newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to participate in Oman trade fairs.
newsitem.headline: Israel to participate in Oman trade fairs.

text.p: The Israel Export Institute said on Wednesday it would participate in three trade exhibitions in Oman in March and April after receiving an official invitation from the Arab Gulf sultanate.
The institute said Israeli participation in the trade fairs would strengthen the peace process between the states.

"The Export Institute intends to participate in these exhibitions despite the short amount of time for organising in order to contribute to strengthening economic ties between Israel and the Gulf states that have lately revived," it said.

The statement said it received invitations to the Muscat fairs this week. The exhibitions were: "woman's world", opening on March 3; "water", set for March 9-12; and "computers and communications" on April 7-10.
Oman and Qatar had raced ahead of other Arab Gulf states in establishing economic ties with Israel in the wake of a 1993 peace deal between the Jewish state and the Palestine Liberation Organisation.
The two energy-rich Gulf states stopped short of full diplomatic ties pending a resolution of all Arab-Israeli conflicts.

But ties were strained after right-wing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took office in June. Oman and Qatar froze normalisation pending a commitment by Netanyahu to implement peace deals signed by the government he ousted.

The pall began to lift in January when Netanyahu handed over most of the West Bank town of Hebron to PLO self-rule. At the end of January, Israel's Maariv newspaper said a Netanyahu aide visited Qatar and possibly Oman during a secret 24-hour mission.

On Tuesday, Israel's Jerusalem Post daily quoted the president of Israel's Koor Industries as saying Koor planned to send a delegation of investors to a Gulf state later this year. Koor President Benjamin Gaon gave no further details.
